en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn one small word with three big jobs: can. Let's start!

steps.title: What you can do
steps.text: In Indonesian you say 'bisa'. In English the word is **can**, and it's very easy to use.
steps.body:
Put **can** before a verb in its base form: **I can swim.** The negative is **can't** (or **cannot**, one word): **I can't swim.**
Can is the same for every subject: **she can**, not 'she cans'. And there is no **to** after it: **I can swim**, not 'I can to swim'.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pak Hasan has a small workshop in Bandung. Which sentence is correct?

options: Pak Hasan can to fix motorbikes.
question.explanation: **Can** never changes: no -s with he/she, even though Pak Hasan = he. And the verb comes straight after it, with no **to**: **can fix**.

steps.title: Can, can't and questions
steps.text: Here are some people talking about what they can and can't do. Notice the questions and short answers.
steps.body:
Questions start with **can**, with no do: **Can you cook?** Short answers: **Yes, I can. / No, I can't.**
Listen for the difference: **can** is short and quiet (almost 'kn'), but **can't** is long and strong.

examples.id: Sari bisa menyanyi dengan sangat bagus.
Nenek saya tidak bisa membaca bahasa Inggris.

examples.en: I can't dance, but I can sing.
examples.id: Saya tidak bisa menari, tapi saya bisa menyanyi.

examples.en: Can you cook? — Yes, I can.
Can Budi play the guitar? — No, he can't.
examples.id: Budi bisa main gitar? — Tidak, dia tidak bisa.

steps.title: Listen: can or can't?
steps.text: Budi is talking about the kitchen. Press play and listen carefully for **can** and **can't**.

question.prompt: Listen to Budi. Which sentence is true?
question.listen: I can't cook, but I can make coffee.
question.explanation: Budi says **I can't cook** (long, strong 'can't') and **I can make coffee** (short, quiet 'can'). So he can make coffee, but he can't cook.

steps.title: Asking for help
steps.text: **Can** has a second job. With **you**, it asks someone to do something for you, like 'tolong' or 'bisa tolong …?'.
steps.body:
Pattern: **Can you** + verb … **please**? This is a request, not a question about ability. Say yes with **Sure!** or **Of course.** Say no with **Sorry, I can't.**
Careful: there is no **do** with can. Say **Can you help me?**, not 'Do you can help me?'.

pairs.en: Can you pass the salt, please?

steps.title: Build a request
steps.text: You're at the office and you need a file from your colleague Rina. Ask her politely.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Bisa tolong kirim filenya ke saya?
question.solution: Can you send me the file, please?
question.explanation: A request is **Can you** + verb + **please**? The order is **Can you send me the file, please?** Please usually goes at the end.

steps.title: Asking permission
steps.text: And the third job: with **I**, can asks for permission, like 'boleh saya …?'.
steps.body:
Pattern: **Can I** + verb …? To say yes: **Yes, you can. / Sure. / Of course.** To say no: **Sorry, you can't.**
Answer with **you**, not I: the other person asks about themselves.
Rules and signs use the same words: **You can't smoke here.**

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Your child is sick, so you want to leave work early today. What do you ask your manager?

question.prompt: Choose the best question for your manager.
options: Can I go home early today?
Do I can go home early today?
Can you go home early today?
question.explanation: You ask permission for yourself, so use **Can I** …? There is no **do** with can, and **Can you** …? asks the manager to do something.

steps.title: Say yes
steps.text: Now you give permission. Your classmate Rina needs a pen.

question.prompt: Rina asks: 'Can I borrow your pen?' You say yes. Choose the best answer.
question.explanation: Rina asks about herself (**Can I**), so you answer with **you**: **Sure, you can.** 'Yes, I can' talks about you, and 'Yes, you do' answers a do-question.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip the cards. Say the meaning before you check.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for when you need help or permission!

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · can
artifact.intro: One word, three jobs: ability, requests and permission. Can + base verb, the same for everyone.
rows: Can you cook? — Yes, I can. / No, I can't.
Can you help me, please? — Sure!
Can I come in? — Yes, you can.
Sorry, you can't. / You can't smoke here.
tips: No **to** and no **-s**: I can swim, she can swim.
No **do** with can: **Can you help me?**, not 'Do you can help me?'.
Answer **Can I …?** with **you**: Yes, you can.

examples.en: Can you pass the salt, please?

steps.title: Watch and practise
steps.text: Want more? Watch a video lesson about can and can't, and try the British Council exercises.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar satu kata kecil dengan tiga tugas besar: can. Ayo mulai!

steps.title: Apa yang bisa kamu lakukan
steps.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita bilang 'bisa'. Dalam bahasa Inggris katanya **can**, dan cara pakainya mudah sekali.
steps.body:
Letakkan **can** sebelum kata kerja bentuk dasar: **I can swim.** Bentuk negatifnya **can't** (atau **cannot**, satu kata): **I can't swim.**
Can sama untuk semua subjek: **she can**, bukan 'she cans'. Dan tidak ada **to** sesudahnya: **I can swim**, bukan 'I can to swim'.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pak Hasan punya bengkel kecil di Bandung. Kalimat mana yang benar?

options: Pak Hasan can to fix motorbikes.
question.explanation: **Can** tidak pernah berubah: tanpa -s untuk he/she, walaupun Pak Hasan = he. Dan kata kerjanya langsung sesudahnya, tanpa **to**: **can fix**.

steps.title: Can, can't dan pertanyaan
steps.text: Ini beberapa orang yang bercerita tentang apa yang bisa dan tidak bisa mereka lakukan. Perhatikan pertanyaan dan jawaban singkatnya.
steps.body:
Pertanyaan dimulai dengan **can**, tanpa do: **Can you cook?** Jawaban singkat: **Yes, I can. / No, I can't.**
Dengarkan bedanya: **can** pendek dan pelan (hampir 'kn'), tapi **can't** panjang dan tegas.

examples.id: Sari bisa menyanyi dengan sangat bagus.
Nenek saya tidak bisa membaca bahasa Inggris.

examples.en: I can't dance, but I can sing.
examples.id: Saya tidak bisa menari, tapi saya bisa menyanyi.

examples.en: Can you cook? — Yes, I can.
Can Budi play the guitar? — No, he can't.
examples.id: Budi bisa main gitar? — Tidak, dia tidak bisa.

steps.title: Dengar: can atau can't?
steps.text: Budi bercerita tentang dapur. Tekan play dan dengarkan baik-baik **can** dan **can't**.

question.prompt: Dengarkan Budi. Kalimat mana yang benar?
question.listen: I can't cook, but I can make coffee.
question.explanation: Budi bilang **I can't cook** ('can't' panjang dan tegas) dan **I can make coffee** ('can' pendek dan pelan). Jadi dia bisa membuat kopi, tapi tidak bisa memasak.

steps.title: Minta tolong
steps.text: **Can** punya tugas kedua. Dengan **you**, can dipakai untuk meminta orang melakukan sesuatu, seperti 'tolong' atau 'bisa tolong …?'.
steps.body:
Polanya: **Can you** + kata kerja … **please**? Ini permintaan, bukan pertanyaan tentang kemampuan. Untuk bilang ya: **Sure!** atau **Of course.** Untuk bilang tidak: **Sorry, I can't.**
Hati-hati: tidak ada **do** kalau memakai can. Ucapkan **Can you help me?**, bukan 'Do you can help me?'.

pairs.en: Can you pass the salt, please?

steps.title: Susun permintaannya
steps.text: Kamu di kantor dan butuh file dari rekan kerjamu, Rina. Minta dengan sopan.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Bisa tolong kirim filenya ke saya?
question.solution: Can you send me the file, please?
question.explanation: Permintaan memakai pola **Can you** + kata kerja + **please**? Urutannya **Can you send me the file, please?** Please biasanya di akhir.

steps.title: Minta izin
steps.text: Dan tugas ketiga: dengan **I**, can dipakai untuk minta izin, seperti 'boleh saya …?'.
steps.body:
Polanya: **Can I** + kata kerja …? Untuk bilang ya: **Yes, you can. / Sure. / Of course.** Untuk bilang tidak: **Sorry, you can't.**
Jawab dengan **you**, bukan I: orang itu bertanya tentang dirinya sendiri.
Aturan dan tanda juga memakai kata yang sama: **You can't smoke here.**

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Anakmu sakit, jadi kamu mau pulang kerja lebih awal hari ini. Apa yang kamu tanyakan ke manajermu?

question.prompt: Pilih pertanyaan yang paling tepat untuk manajermu.
options: Can I go home early today?
Do I can go home early today?
Can you go home early today?
question.explanation: Kamu minta izin untuk dirimu sendiri, jadi pakai **Can I** …? Tidak ada **do** kalau memakai can, dan **Can you** …? meminta manajer melakukan sesuatu.

steps.title: Bilang ya
steps.text: Sekarang kamu yang memberi izin. Teman sekelasmu, Rina, butuh pulpen.

question.prompt: Rina bertanya: 'Can I borrow your pen?' Kamu mengizinkan. Pilih jawaban yang paling tepat.
question.explanation: Rina bertanya tentang dirinya (**Can I**), jadi jawab dengan **you**: **Sure, you can.** 'Yes, I can' membicarakan dirimu, dan 'Yes, you do' adalah jawaban untuk pertanyaan dengan do.

steps.title: Ulangan cepat
steps.text: Balik kartunya. Sebutkan artinya sebelum kamu cek.

steps.title: Contekan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk saat kamu butuh bantuan atau izin!
